Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.220/03babb9661b2a9b6ac29ab8901c6b8c1/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

14	
15	```css
16	.viz-root {
17	  color-scheme: light;
18	  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
19	  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
20	  --text-secondary: #52514e;
21	  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
22	  /* …only the roles this chart uses */
23	}
24	@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
25	  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
26	    color-scheme: dark;
27	    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
28	    --text-primary:   #ffffff;

30	    --series-1:       #3987e5;
31	  }
32	}
33	:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
34	  color-scheme: dark;
35	  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
36	  --text-primary:   #ffffff;
37	  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
38	  --series-1:       #3987e5;
39	}
40	```
41	
42	Declare the dark values under both scopes as above — the media query covers
43	the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
44	which must win both ways (the `:not(…)` guard lets a light stamp beat
45	OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).

47	## Categorical palette
48	
49	Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
50	dark surface, not a separate palette:
51	
52	| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
53	|------|-----|-------|------|
54	| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
55	| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
56	| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
57	| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
58	| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
59	| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
60	| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
61	| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
62	
63	This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
64	pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
65	(OKLab ×100, ≥8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 19.6 light / 19.3
66	dark (≥15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
67	multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors — with all 28 pairs in
68	play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
69	re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule — so those
70	chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
71	in both modes** (worst pair CVD ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
72	light / 20.9 dark — clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
73	facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
74	together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
75	light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
76	sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
77	visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
78	dark band (OKLCH L ≈ 0.48–0.67, ≥ 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
79	set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening —
80	the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
81	changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
82	dark run in the 6–8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
83	this order deliberately trades that fourth slot — yellow now sits beside orange —
84	for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow↔orange
85	confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
86	pure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full
87	gate.
88	
89	The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic — candidate
90	orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
91	modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
92	passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
93	your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
94	choose only among the passing ones.
95	
96	## Sequential hue
97	
98	Default single hue: **blue**, light→dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
99	once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
100	one-hue ramp.
101	
102	| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
103	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
104	| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
105	| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
106	| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
107	| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |
108	
109	The full 100→700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude —
110	heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
111	to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks —
112	funnel stages, tiers — validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
113	must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
114	2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).
115	
116	## Diverging pair
117	
118	**blue ↔ red** — warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
119	(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue↔aqua was
120	rejected — both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)
121	
122	## Status palette (fixed — never themed)
123	
124	| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
127	| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
128	| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
129	| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |
130	
131	Dark: same four steps — all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
132	distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
133	serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
134	a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
135	from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series —
136	distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
137	carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
138	(unsimulated ΔE ≥ 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
139	below 15 — in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
140	4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text
141	green `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)
142	holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
143	same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
144	placement; never on hue alone.
145	
146	## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)
147	
148	One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
149	tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
150	*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
151	Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` — never
152	decorative, never on by default.
153	
154	## Surfaces (for the validator)
155	
156	- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
157	- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`
158	
159	These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
160	palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
161	`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` —
162	contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
163	actually renders on.
164	
165	## Chart chrome & ink
166	
167	| Role | Light | Dark |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
170	| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
171	| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#ffffff` |
172	| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
173	| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
174	| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
175	| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
176	| Delta ↑ good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
177	| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |
178	
179	## Filter controls
180	
181	Filters are standard UI, not chart components — the chart layer only adds the
182	composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
183	rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
184	bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
185	footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.
186	
187	## Typeface & figures
188	
189	Everything — including the hero figure — stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
190	-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
191	standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
192	figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
193	vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.

# Reference palette

This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
is system-agnostic — **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.

## How to use these values

Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
reference them by role throughout — so the light/dark values swap in one place,
and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:

```css
.viz-root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
  --text-secondary: #52514e;
  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
  /* …only the roles this chart uses */
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
    --text-primary:   #ffffff;
    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
    --series-1:       #3987e5;
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
  --text-primary:   #ffffff;
  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
  --series-1:       #3987e5;
}
```

Declare the dark values under both scopes as above — the media query covers
the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
which must win both ways (the `:not(…)` guard lets a light stamp beat
OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).

## Categorical palette

Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
dark surface, not a separate palette:

| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
|------|-----|-------|------|
| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |

This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
(OKLab ×100, ≥8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 19.6 light / 19.3
dark (≥15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors — with all 28 pairs in
play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule — so those
chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
in both modes** (worst pair CVD ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
light / 20.9 dark — clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
dark band (OKLCH L ≈ 0.48–0.67, ≥ 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening —
the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
dark run in the 6–8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
this order deliberately trades that fourth slot — yellow now sits beside orange —
for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow↔orange
confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
pure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full
gate.

The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic — candidate
orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
choose only among the passing ones.

## Sequential hue

Default single hue: **blue**, light→dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
one-hue ramp.

| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |

The full 100→700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude —
heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks —
funnel stages, tiers — validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).

## Diverging pair

**blue ↔ red** — warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue↔aqua was
rejected — both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)

## Status palette (fixed — never themed)

| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
|---|---|---|---|
| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |

Dark: same four steps — all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series —
distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
(unsimulated ΔE ≥ 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
below 15 — in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text
green `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)
holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
placement; never on hue alone.

## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)

One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` — never
decorative, never on by default.

## Surfaces (for the validator)

- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`

These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` —
contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
actually renders on.

## Chart chrome & ink

| Role | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#ffffff` |
| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
| Delta ↑ good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |

## Filter controls

Filters are standard UI, not chart components — the chart layer only adds the
composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.

## Typeface & figures

Everything — including the hero figure — stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.

29	when the categories have no natural order (products, teams, endpoints).

31	information the chart already shows, and fails the categorical checks by design
32	(a ramp spans the lightness band and drops below the chroma floor).

42	fails this (both cool); blue↔red or blue↔orange succeed (warm/cool).
43	✅ Two hues that read as opposite + a neutral gray midpoint.

46	✅ Status tokens only when the color *means* good/bad; categorical when it's identity.

# Anti-patterns — what goes wrong

Check every chart against this list. If your output matches an entry, it is wrong —
fix it before shipping. These are real failure modes, each caught in shipping
dashboards.

## Color & encoding

**❌ Dual-axis charts (two y-scales on one plot).**
Why it misleads: the alignment of the two scales is arbitrary, so the chart invents a
correlation that isn't in the data. Real example: an "Adoption" chart plotting Users
(0–30k) against Sessions (0–800k) — a reviewer flagged it as looking "hallucinated."
✅ Do instead: two charts, small multiples, or index both series to a common base
(=100 at t0) on **one** axis.

**❌ Recolor-on-filter.** Assigning colors by current rank, so filtering out a series
repaints the survivors.
Why: a reader who learned "Acme is blue" is now misled.
✅ Color follows the entity, not its row number. Survivors keep their hue.

**❌ Cycling / generating hues past 8.** A 9th categorical color, generated or reused.
Why: indistinguishable from an existing slot under CVD; breaks the order check.
✅ Fold the tail into "Other," facet into small multiples, or use composite encoding.

**❌ Eyeballing colorblind-safety.** "These look different enough."
✅ Run `scripts/validate_palette.js`. Adjacent ΔE ≥ 8 (OKLab ×100), or 6–8 WITH secondary encoding.

**❌ A value-ramp on nominal categories.** Coloring each bar darker-where-bigger
when the categories have no natural order (products, teams, endpoints).
Why: it double-encodes bar length as hue, burns the only free channel on
information the chart already shows, and fails the categorical checks by design
(a ramp spans the lightness band and drops below the chroma floor).
✅ One series → one color (slot 1) for every bar. Ordered categories (funnel,
tiers, age bands) → the ordinal ramp, validated with `--ordinal`.

**❌ Rainbow / non-neighbor sequential.** A multi-hue ramp for magnitude.
✅ One hue, light→dark. (Analogous neighbors or semantic heat are the only multi-hue
sequential exceptions, always with a scale legend.)

**❌ A hue at the diverging midpoint, or two cool hues as the two poles.**
Why: the midpoint must read as "nothing"; poles must read as opposite. blue↔aqua
fails this (both cool); blue↔red or blue↔orange succeed (warm/cool).
✅ Two hues that read as opposite + a neutral gray midpoint.

**❌ Status color used for a non-status series** (or a series color used for status).
✅ Status tokens only when the color *means* good/bad; categorical when it's identity.

## Form

**❌ Eight categorical hues when the story is one number.** The most common way a
chart misses its point.
✅ Emphasis (highlight one, gray the rest), or a stat tile / hero number.

**❌ A one-bar bar chart, or a 2-slice pie.**
✅ A stat tile. The number is the chart.

**❌ A donut/pie for comparing close values.**
✅ A bar, or the numbers. Part-to-whole at a glance only, ≤ 6 segments.

**❌ More than ~7 color classes carrying meaning.**
✅ A table, or table + chart. Past ~7 bins, adjacent classes blur.

## Marks & chrome

**❌ Thick saturated blocks, heavy gridlines, no breathing room.** Reads loud, even
childish, at scale.
✅ Thin marks, hairline recessive grid/axes, generous padding. Saturated fills are
for small marks and accents, never large blocks.

**❌ Dashed gridlines or axis rules.** Dashing adds visual noise and reads as
"projection" or "threshold" when it's just a grid.
✅ Gridlines and axes are solid hairlines, one shade off the surface.

**❌ A number on every data point.** A value beside every dot or segment is chaos and goes unread.
✅ A legend is always present for ≥ 2 series; direct-label *selectively* (the endpoint, the extreme, the one series that matters) and let the axis + tooltip carry the rest.

**❌ A border drawn around marks to separate them.**
✅ A 2px surface gap between fills (stacked segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring (on overlapping markers).

**❌ A label clipped by, or overflowing, a too-small bar or stacked segment** —
including `overflow: hidden` cropping the first/last characters of an in-segment label.
✅ Only render a label inside a mark when it fits with padding; otherwise move it
outside the bar end, or drop it to the tooltip/legend (the value stays in the table view).

**❌ A chart container whose fixed height excludes the x-axis band** — the plot
fits, the axis labels don't, so the card gets a tiny nested vertical scroll.
✅ Size the container to include the axis labels (plot height + x-axis band),
or let the container grow with its content instead of fixing a height.

**❌ A display or serif face on the hero figure.** It reads as off-brand decoration.
✅ The hero figure uses the same sans as everything else.

**❌ `tabular-nums` on a large standalone number.** Equal-width digits make `121`
look loose at display sizes.
✅ Proportional figures on hero and stat-tile values; `tabular-nums` only where
numbers align vertically (table rows, axis ticks).

**❌ Texture on by default, or as decoration.** Dense angled fields are a vestibular
risk and read as noise on value scales.
✅ Texture is opt-in (a11y setting, print, forced-colors), 45°/135° only, ordered on
value scales.

## Interaction & accessibility

**❌ A tooltip as the only way to read a value.**
✅ Tooltips enhance, never gate — every value is also reachable via direct labels or
the table view; keyboard focus shows the same as hover.

**❌ Pinpoint hover targets — an 8px scatter dot you must land on dead-center.**
✅ The hit area includes the 2px gap and meets a ~24px minimum; dense scatter uses a nearest-point / Voronoi layer.

**❌ Per-chart filters, or filters inside a chart card.**
✅ One filter row above everything it scopes; all charts re-render against the same slice.

**❌ Skeleton flash on refetch.**
✅ Hold the previous render at reduced opacity — no layout jump.

**❌ No table view / color-only encoding on a continuous scale.**
✅ Every chart has a table-view twin (the WCAG-clean equivalent).

      fruitLimit: 3,
      fruitDelay: 14,
      trees: 8,
      blueStart: 18,
      redStart: 5,
      seed: 90210,
    },
  },
]

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

  blueVision: number // sensing radius
  blueCopy: number // energy needed to make a copy

  redUpkeep: number
  redSpeed: number
  redVision: number
  redStrength: number // energy moved per contact

  redPause: number // seconds resting after a contact

export const PARAM_SPECS: Record<ParamKey, ParamSpec> = Object.fromEntries(
  PARAM_GROUPS.flatMap((g) => g.specs).map((s) => [s.key, s]),
) as Record<ParamKey, ParamSpec>

export type Preset = {
  id: string
  name: string
  blurb: string
  params: Params
}

export const PRESETS: Preset[] = [

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

export type Params = {
  // Fruit
  fruitGrowth: number // fruit grown per second, per tree
  fruitLimit: number // fruit a tree can hold at once
  fruitDelay: number // seconds a tree sulks after being picked

  // Blue blobs (fruit eaters)
  blueUpkeep: number // energy burnt per second at full speed
  blueSpeed: number // world units per second
  blueVision: number // sensing radius
  blueCopy: number // energy needed to make a copy
  blueEatTime: number // seconds spent chewing

  // Red blobs (contact feeders)
  redUpkeep: number
  redSpeed: number
  redVision: number
  redStrength: number // energy moved per contact
  redCopy: number
  redPause: number // seconds resting after a contact

  // World setup (applied on reset)
  trees: number
  blueStart: number
  redStart: number
  worldSize: number // dish radius in world units
  seed: number
}

export type ParamKey = keyof Params

export type ParamSpec = {
  key: ParamKey
  label: string
  min: number
  max: number
  step: number
  unit?: string
  hint: string
  /** Setup params only take effect on reset. */
  setup?: boolean
  integer?: boolean
}

export const DEFAULT_PARAMS: Params = {
  fruitGrowth: 0.2,
  fruitLimit: 8,
  fruitDelay: 4,

  blueUpkeep: 2.6,
  blueSpeed: 24,
  blueVision: 90,
  blueCopy: 78,
  blueEatTime: 1.6,

  redUpkeep: 2,
  redSpeed: 29,

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

tool_use_result.originalFile:
export type Kind = 'blue' | 'red'

/** What a blob is doing right now. Drives both behaviour and the inspector. */
export type Action =
  | 'wander'
  | 'seek' // blue: heading for a tree with fruit
  | 'eat' // blue: locked, chewing
  | 'flee' // blue: a red blob is too close
  | 'avoid' // blue: shoving out of a crowded patch
  | 'gather' // blue: drifting toward a tree with nothing ripe yet
  | 'hunt' // red: closing on a blue blob
  | 'contact' // red: locked, the contact moment
  | 'rest' // red: locked, resting it off

export type Traits = {
  speed: number
  vision: number
  thrift: number
}

export type Blob = {
  id: number
  kind: Kind
  x: number
  y: number
  /** Position at the start of the current step, for render interpolation. */
  px: number
  py: number
  vx: number
  vy: number
  energy: number
  age: number
  lifespan: number
  action: Action
  /** Seconds left on a locked action (eat / contact / rest). 0 when free. */
  actionTimer: number
  actionTotal: number
  copyCooldown: number
  targetTree: number
  targetBlob: number
  /** Blue only: grace period after a contact. Red cannot touch it again yet. */
  immunity: number
  /** Blue only: startled burst of speed and nerve after a contact. */
  panic: number
  traits: Traits
  generation: number
  parentId: number
  bornAt: number
  /** Fruit eaten (blue) or contacts made (red). */
  meals: number
  children: number
  // Presentation only — never read by the rules.
  phase: number
  blinkTimer: number
  blinkFor: number
  squash: number
  glow: number
}

export type Tree = {
  id: number
  x: number
  y: number
  scale: number
  /** Whole fruit hanging on the tree right now. */
  fruit: number
  /** Progress toward the next fruit, 0..1. */
  growth: number
  /** Seconds before ripening resumes after a pick. */
  delay: number
  anchors: { x: number; y: number; z: number; r: number }[]
  /** Per-anchor pop-in scale, 0..1. */
  pop: number[]
  leanSeed: number
}

export type EffectKind = 'eat' | 'contact' | 'birth' | 'death' | 'ripen'

export type Effect = {
  kind: EffectKind
  x: number
  y: number
  z: number
  life: number
  maxLife: number
  color: Kind | 'fruit'
  seed: number
}

export type Counts = {
  fruit: number
  blue: number
  red: number
}

export type World = {
  t: number
  steps: number
  radius: number
  trees: Tree[]
  blobs: Blob[]
  nextId: number
  effects: Effect[]
  counts: Counts
  /** Running tallies, useful for the summary. */
  totals: {
    births: { blue: number; red: number }
    deaths: { blue: number; red: number }
    starved: { blue: number; red: number }
    aged: { blue: number; red: number }
    fruitEaten: number
    contacts: number
  }
  extinct: { blue: number | null; red: number | null }
  capReached: boolean
}

export type Params = {
  // Fruit
  fruitGrowth: number // fruit grown per second, per tree
  fruitLimit: number // fruit a tree can hold at once
  fruitDelay: number // seconds a tree sulks after being picked

  // Blue blobs (fruit eaters)
  blueUpkeep: number // energy burnt per second at full speed
  blueSpeed: number // world units per second
  blueVision: number // sensing radius
  blueCopy: number // energy needed to make a copy
  blueEatTime: number // seconds spent chewing

  // Red blobs (contact feeders)
  redUpkeep: number
  redSpeed: number
  redVision: number
  redStrength: number // energy moved per contact
  redCopy: number
  redPause: number // seconds resting after a contact

  // World setup (applied on reset)
  trees: number
  blueStart: number
  redStart: number
  worldSize: number // dish radius in world units
  seed: number
}

export type ParamKey = keyof Params

export type ParamSpec = {
  key: ParamKey
  label: string
  min: number
  max: number
  step: number
  unit?: string
  hint: string
  /** Setup params only take effect on reset. */
  setup?: boolean
  integer?: boolean
}

export const DEFAULT_PARAMS: Params = {
  fruitGrowth: 0.2,

  blueUpkeep: 2.6,

    specs: [
      {

  PARAM_GROUPS.flatMap((g) => g.specs).map((s) => [s.key, s]),

}

      fruitLimit: 9,

      seed: 424242,
    },

  {
    id: 'low-fruit',
    name: 'Low-fruit garden',
    blurb: 'Thin food supply keeps every group small.',
    params: {
      ...DEFAULT_PARAMS,
      fruitGrowth: 0.02,
      fruitLimit: 3,
      fruitDelay: 14,
      trees: 8,
      blueStart: 18,
      redStart: 5,
      seed: 90210,
    },
  },
]

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user gave a single, detailed XML-structured brief to build a **playful living-garden simulator** — a "cute animated ecology toy." Full intent:

   - **`<brief>`**: A small round world with fruit trees, blue blobs, and red blobs. User tunes rules, presses play, watches the three groups rise and fall. Should feel like a tabletop world with moving bean-shaped characters, visible fruit, live controls, and charts that tell the story.
   - **`<freedom>`**: Creative freedom over layout, controls, visuals, algorithms, technical approach. "This prompt gives direction, not a strict checklist. The important part is that the world feels alive, the numbers come from the simulation, and the user can understand cause and effect."
   - **`<world>`**: Round 3D-looking map like a tiny raised garden dish; draggable to rotate; trees/bushes with green fruit; blue and red glossy oval blobs with simple faces; soft shadows, depth, bouncing, blinking, leaning, personality; click a blob to inspect. Food attached to plants — when a blob uses fruit the plant visibly has less, then regrows.
   - **`<simulation>`**: Each blob has energy. Moving uses energy; waiting uses a little; blue restores from fruit; red restores after gentle contact with blue; making a new blob uses stored energy; fruit returns slowly. Must create natural waves (more fruit → more blue; more blue → more red; too many red → blue drops; blue rare → red fades). **"Do not fake the chart curves. The waves should come from the energy rules."**
   - **`<motion>`**: Blobs visibly choose actions. Blue: look for fruit, gather near trees, wander, avoid crowded areas, move away from red. Red: look for blue, wander when none near, pause after contact. Eating/contact get short cute animations (pause, chew, bounce, glow, sparkle, fruit shrink, energy pulse) and these pauses must affect behavior so actions can't instantly repeat.
   - **`<controls>`**: Fruit growth speed, fruit limit, fruit return delay, blue energy use/speed/vision/copy threshold/eating time, red energy use/speed/vision/contact strength/copy threshold/pause time, starting fruit trees/blue/red, world size, random seed, simulation speed. Plus play, pause, step, reset, randomize, and presets: balanced garden, fruit-rich garden, red-heavy garden, fragile balance, low-fruit garden.
   - **`<charts>`**: Real charts from recorded history. Main chart shows fruit + blue + red on one timeline with readable scaling keeping all three visible. Extras: blue-vs-red phase plot, run summary, trait trends if blobs inherit traits. Summary can say things like "The garden stayed balanced", "Blue blobs grew first, then red blobs followed", "Low fruit kept the garden small", "One group faded and the world settled into a simpler state."
   - **`<inspection>`**: Clicking a blob shows group color, energy, age, current action, speed, sensing range, time left in eating/pause animation, traits/family info.
   - **`<quality>`**: Must demonstrate long-running waves; a fruit-rich setting where blue grows quickly; a low-fruit setting where the garden stays small; a red-heavy setting where blue dips first and red fades later; group sizes that level out instead of growing forever. Prioritize believable emergent behavior, clear controls, readable charts, charming map animation.

   **Explicit constraints (must be preserved):**
   - "Work only inside the current working directory. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."
   - "During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9217, then use that port for runtime verification."
   - "Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm."
   - "Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title." → Title is exactly **"Opus 5"** in both places, nothing appended.
   - "Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."

   Also from global CLAUDE.md: **NEVER use `rm -rf`** — use `trash` instead.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript 6, pnpm, port 9217 (`strictPort` on both `server` and `preview`).
   - Deterministic seeded simulation: mulberry32 RNG, fixed timestep `DT = 1/30`, stable iteration order, separate RNG streams for world creation (`seed`) and stepping (`seed ^ 0x9e3779b9`).
   - Spatial hash grid for neighbor queries (`Grid` class, cell = vision/1.5).
   - Agent behavior state machine with locked actions (eat/contact/rest) and steering (smooth velocity lerp, `turnRate`, rim sliding).
   - Predator–prey ecology theory applied deliberately: Lotka–Volterra instability, **paradox of enrichment**, Holling type-II functional response, **handling time** (redPause), **prey refuge** (canopy shelter), **Beddington–DeAngelis predator mutual interference** (crowding-based upkeep penalty), landscape-of-fear collapse, hunger-modulated risk-taking.
   - Inheritable traits (speed, vision, thrift) with mutation for trait-trend charts.
   - History with adaptive decimation (halve resolution when full, keeps whole run on one timeline).
   - Analysis: moving average, prominence-filtered peak finding, cross-correlation for phase lag, narrative summary generation.
   - `dataviz` skill rules: **never dual-axis** (index to a common base or use small multiples), validated palette, legend always for ≥2 series, selective direct labels, hairline solid gridlines, table-view twin, hover crosshair/tooltip, 2px surface gaps, `tabular-nums` only in aligned columns.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`index.html`** — set `<title>Opus 5</title>`, added `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark" />`. Required by the title constraint.
   - **`vite.config.ts`** — port config:
     ```ts
     export default defineConfig({
       plugins: [react()],
       server: { port: 9217, strictPort: true },
       preview: { port: 9217, strictPort: true },
     })
     ```
   - **`src/sim/rng.ts`** — `Rng` class (mulberry32): `next()`, `range(min,max)`, `int()`, `normal()` (sum of 3 uniforms), `inDisc(radius)`.
   - **`src/sim/types.ts`** — `Kind = 'blue'|'red'`; `Action = 'wander'|'seek'|'eat'|'flee'|'avoid'|'gather'|'hunt'|'contact'|'rest'`; `Traits {speed,vision,thrift}`; `Blob` (id, kind, x, y, px, py, vx, vy, energy, age, lifespan, action, actionTimer, actionTotal, copyCooldown, targetTree, targetBlob, **immunity**, **panic**, **sheltered**, **crowding**, traits, generation, parentId, bornAt, meals, children, phase, blinkTimer, blinkFor, squash, glow); `Tree` (id, x, y, scale, fruit, growth, delay, anchors[{x,y,z,r}], pop[], leanSeed); `Effect`; `Counts`; `World` (t, steps, radius, trees, blobs, nextId, effects, counts, totals{births,deaths,starved,aged,fruitEaten,contacts}, extinct, capReached).
   - **`src/sim/params.ts`** — `Params` type + `PARAM_GROUPS` (Fruit / Blue blobs / Red blobs / World setup) with labels, min/max/step, hints, `setup` flags. Current `DEFAULT_PARAMS`:
     ```ts
     fruitGrowth: 0.2, fruitLimit: 8, fruitDelay: 4,
     blueUpkeep: 2.6, blueSpeed: 24, blueVision: 90, blueCopy: 78, blueEatTime: 1.6,
     redUpkeep: 1.4, redSpeed: 29, redVision: 95, redStrength: 12, redCopy: 84, redPause: 4,
     trees: 20, blueStart: 30, redStart: 8, worldSize: 330, seed: 20260725,
     ```
     `PRESETS` array with 5 entries (balanced, fruit-rich, red-heavy, fragile, low-fruit) — **these preset param overrides were written early and have NOT been re-tuned since the ecology was reworked.** `redStrength` spec range changed to min 2 / max 40 with hint "Energy a blue blob loses per contact. Red gains half again as much from the exchange."
   - **`src/sim/world.ts`** — the heart. `DT = 1/30`. Current `CONST`:
     ```ts
     maxEnergy: 120, fruitEnergy: 34, contactEfficiency: 1.9, birthCost: 0.12,
     copyCooldown: 7, contactTime: 0.5, contactImmunity: 2.6,
     panicTime: 2.2, panicSpeed: 1.14, panicRange: 1.55,
     shelterRadius: 26, shelterFactor: 0.3,
     interferenceRange: 72, interferenceCost: 0.34,
     blobRadius: 7, eatReach: 12, contactReach: 12, idleUpkeep: 0.4,
     threatFactor: 0.62, hungerNerve: 0.72, turnRate: 7, separationRange: 26,
     populationCap: 900, blueLifespan: 210, redLifespan: 330, lifespanSpread: 0.22,
     mutation: 0.05, traitMin: 0.5, traitMax: 1.8,
     ```
     Key mechanisms:
     - Shelter pre-pass inside `step()` (before the per-blob loop) sets `b.sheltered` for blue blobs within `shelterRadius` of any tree.
     - Upkeep with red interference: `const jostle = b.kind === 'red' ? 1 + CONST.interferenceCost * b.crowding : 1; const upkeep = ((blue?blueUpkeep:redUpkeep) * jostle) / b.traits.thrift;` then `b.energy -= upkeep * (idleUpkeep + (1-idleUpkeep)*speedFrac) * dt`.
     - `stepBlue` hunger/fear: `const hunger = 1 - clamp(b.energy/(maxEnergy*0.7)); const nerve = 1 - hungerNerve*hunger; const threatRange = vision*threatFactor*nerve*(startled?panicRange:1)`.
     - Blue picks fruit at eat start (`tree.fruit--; tree.delay = params.fruitDelay`), then chews for `blueEatTime`, gaining `fruitEnergy` in `finishLockedAction`.
     - `stepRed` target scoring: `const reach = o.sheltered && o.action !== 'eat' ? vision*shelterFactor : vision;` skip if beyond reach or `o.immunity > 0`; `score = 1 - d/vision; if (o.action==='eat') score += 1.2; else if (gather||seek) score += 0.2; if (o.id===b.targetBlob) score += 0.18`.
     - On contact: `taken = min(redStrength, max(0, prey.energy)); prey.energy -= redStrength; prey.immunity = contactImmunity; prey.panic = panicTime; if (prey.action==='eat') { prey.action='flee'; prey.actionTimer=0 }; b.energy = min(maxEnergy, b.energy + taken*contactEfficiency)`; red goes `contact` (0.5s) → `rest` (redPause) → `wander`.
     - `countCrowding(b, grid)` called at the top of `stepRed`.
     - `tryCopy`: `share = (b.energy*(1-birthCost))/2`, parent and child each get `share`, both get `copyCooldown`, traits mutated via `mutate()`.
   - **`src/sim/history.ts`** — `Sample` type (t, fruit, blue, red, blueEnergy, redEnergy, blue/red Speed/Vision/Thrift means), `History` class with `maybeSample`, decimation at MAX_SAMPLES 1400, BASE_INTERVAL 0.5.
   - **`src/sim/analysis.ts`** — `movingAverage`, `findPeaks(values, prominence)`, `mean`, `stdev`, `bestLag(a,b,maxLag)` (returns null if r ≤ 0.25), and `summarise({samples, fruitCapacity, blueAlive, redAlive})` → `RunSummary {headline, notes[], cycles, lagSeconds, settled, tone}` with the narrative branches the brief asked for.
   - **`src/sim/engine.ts`** — `Engine` class: `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`/`notify` (for `useSyncExternalStore`), `reset`, `setParam`, `setParams`, `setRunning`, `setSpeed`, `select`, `selected()`, `stepOnce()`, `advance(realSeconds)` (accumulator, `REALTIME_STEPS = 1/DT`, per-frame step cap, returns interpolation alpha), `run(seconds)` for headless.
   - **`scripts/probe.ts`** — headless tuner. Flags: `--seconds`, `--seeds`, `--preset`, `--sweep key=v1,v2,...`, `--trace`. `analyse()` skips the first 12% as transient and reports blue/red mean+range, fruit mean + % of capacity, wave counts via `findPeaks`, lag via `bestLag`, end counts, flags (BLUE-OUT / RED-OUT / CAPPED), and ms. `traceRun()` prints a per-20s table of blue, red, fruit, contacts/20s, eaten/20s, mean red energy, mean blue energy, and the red action histogram.

4. **Errors and fixes:**
   - **Write to existing files failed** ("File has not been read yet") for `vite.config.ts` and `index.html` → Read them first, then Write.
   - **Scratchpad `diag.ts` failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND** due to a long relative import path from the scratchpad into the project → abandoned; replaced with a `--trace` flag inside `scripts/probe.ts` (cleaner, stays a legitimate dev tool).
   - **Red always going extinct (probe #1)** → root cause: `blueVision` (95) > `redVision` (78) meant blues fled before red could sense them. Fixed with `CONST.threatFactor = 0.62` so blue only panics deep inside its own vision.
   - **Red wiping out all blue when made faster** → bistability; addressed over many steps (see Problem Solving).
   - **Blue starving with trees full of fruit** (trace showed 104 starved, fruit rising to 160) → "landscape of fear": permanent fleeing, no eating. Fixed with `hungerNerve` so hungry blobs take risks.
   - **Refuge backfiring** — with `shelterRadius: 40` applied regardless of action, blues hovering at trees during fruit scarcity were permanently hidden and red starved amid plenty. Fixed by tightening to `shelterRadius: 26`, `shelterFactor: 0.3`, and restoring `o.action !== 'eat'` so reaching for fruit breaks cover.
   - **Declared-but-unused `contactCooldownBlue`** in CONST → became the actual fix (`contactImmunity`), since without it a blob surrounded by reds lost all energy in one frame.
   - **Light-mode red↔green CVD warning (ΔE 7.2)** from the palette validator → swapped green to `#00947a`, which passes all checks with no warnings.

5. **Problem Solving:**

   The dominant problem has been making the ecology **actually oscillate without either group going extinct**, since the brief forbids faking the curves. Findings, in order:
   - Sensing asymmetry is required for predation to occur at all (`threatFactor`).
   - Contact lethality must be decoupled from predator gain — `contactEfficiency: 1.9` means red gains ~1.9× what blue loses. This is what lets blue survive several contacts while red still earns a living, and it fits the brief's "gentle contact interaction" framing.
   - Per-prey saturation (`contactImmunity: 2.6s`) prevents a blob from being drained by every nearby red in one frame.
   - Hunger must modulate fear or blue starves amid plenty.
   - A prey refuge is needed, but a too-generous one starves the predator; the working version hides only blobs tucked at a trunk and *not* eating.
   - **Predator mutual interference (`interferenceCost`, `crowding`) is the key stabilizer** — it limits red by its own numbers instead of by driving blue to zero, and it widened the coexistence band substantially. Once red establishes, coexistence with real waves (3 blue / 2–5 red waves over 3000s, lags 585–716s) is now reproducible.
   - **Remaining open problem: red *establishment* is still bimodal by seed.** Red either establishes and then coexists robustly, or fails in the first ~100s and the run becomes a blue-only monoculture (blue ≈ 55, fruit ≈ 1%).
   - Best balance observed with the *latest* constants was **redUpkeep 2.2** (blue 26.9 mean vs red 15.0, blue > red, 3/5 waves, ends 30/20) — but `DEFAULT_PARAMS.redUpkeep` is still **1.4**, left over from an earlier sweep. The final worldSize sweep was therefore run at a mistuned default, which is the most likely explanation for its near-universal blue-out result.

6. **All user messages:**
   - The single user message is the full garden-simulator brief quoted in section 1, including the XML sections `<brief>`, `<freedom>`, `<world>`, `<simulation>`, `<motion>`, `<controls>`, `<charts>`, `<inspection>`, `<quality>`, and these trailing constraints verbatim: *"Work only inside the current working directory. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."* / *"During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9217, then use that port for runtime verification."* / *"Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm."* / *"Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title."* / *"Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."*
   - There were no other user messages. All later inputs were tool results and system reminders (task-tracking nudges, MCP server notices).

7. **Pending Tasks:**
   - Finish tuning so red reliably establishes and coexistence is the default outcome; then re-tune all 5 presets (balanced, fruit-rich, red-heavy, fragile balance, low-fruit) to demonstrate the specific behaviors `<quality>` requires.
   - Build the renderer: canvas 2.5D rotating garden dish (drag to rotate, painter's-algorithm depth sort), trees with attached fruit at anchor points that shrink on pick and pop back on regrowth, glossy bean blobs with faces/blink/lean/bounce/squash, soft shadows, and effects (eat sparkle, contact glow/energy pulse, birth pop, death fade). Render interpolation via `px/py` and the `advance()` alpha.
   - Build the React UI: all 20 controls + sim speed, play/pause/step/reset/randomize, 5 presets, click-to-inspect panel with all fields from `<inspection>`.
   - Build charts per `dataviz` rules: single-axis main chart (fruit + blue + red, indexed to a common base — **no dual axis**), blue-vs-red phase plot, trait trends, run summary from `summarise()`, plus a table view and hover crosshair/tooltip; light+dark themes with the validated palettes.
   - Update `package.json` scripts (dev/preview on 9217, `probe`, `test`), write vitest tests (determinism, no-extinction/oscillation assertions), run typecheck/lint/build, and verify at runtime on port 9217.

8. **Current Work:**

   I was in the middle of tuning the ecology with `scripts/probe.ts`. The immediately preceding step was tightening the canopy refuge:
   ```ts
   shelterRadius: 26,
   shelterFactor: 0.3,
   ```
   and in `stepRed`'s target scan:
   ```ts
   // Tucked against a trunk it is hard to make out. Reaching up into the
   // branches for fruit breaks cover, which is where most contacts happen.
   const reach = o.sheltered && o.action !== 'eat' ? vision * CONST.shelterFactor : vision
   ```
   That sweep (`redUpkeep=1.8,2.2,2.6,3.0`) showed redUpkeep 2.2 seed #0 as the best result — `blue 26.9 ( 2- 75) red 15.0 ( 3- 31) fruit 32.1 20% waves 3/5 lag 585s end 30/20` — with the other seeds red-out.

   The very last command was a `worldSize=190,230,270,330` sweep, run with `DEFAULT_PARAMS.redUpkeep` still at **1.4**. It came back almost entirely BLUE-OUT (e.g. `worldSize=190 #0 ... BLUE-OUT`, `worldSize=270 #1/#2 BLUE-OUT`), with only `worldSize=330 #1` surviving as `blue 34.9 ( 2- 62) red 0.0 ... RED-OUT`. That result is confounded by the stale 1.4 default rather than being a clean read on world size.

9. **Optional Next Step:**

   Set `DEFAULT_PARAMS.redUpkeep` to ~2.2 (the value that produced the best coexistence under the current constants) and re-run the probe across multiple seeds to confirm, then address the remaining red-establishment bimodality — most likely by raising `redStart` and/or starting energy so red reliably survives its first ~100s. This continues the tuning work quoted above, driven by the brief's requirement: *"Do not fake the chart curves. The waves should come from the energy rules."* and *"Run the relevant checks yourself."*

   Concretely, the next command would be a re-sweep in the shape of the ones already being run:
   `pnpm exec tsx scripts/probe.ts --seconds 3000 --seeds 3 --sweep redUpkeep=2.0,2.2,2.4` — followed by a `redStart` sweep to fix establishment, before moving on to the untouched renderer/UI/chart work.

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]

  t: number

  blueEnergy: number

  redSpeed: number

const MAX_SAMPLES = 1400
const BASE_INTERVAL = 0.5

/**
 * Rolling record of the run. When it fills up it halves its own resolution
 * instead of dropping the start, so the whole run stays on one timeline.
 */
export class History {
  samples: Sample[] = []
  interval = BASE_INTERVAL
  private nextAt = 0

  reset() {
    this.samples = []
    this.interval = BASE_INTERVAL
    this.nextAt = 0
  }

  maybeSample(world: World) {
    if (world.t < this.nextAt) return
    this.nextAt = world.t + this.interval

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent:** The user gave a single, detailed XML-structured brief to build a **playful living-garden simulator** — a "cute animated ecology toy." Full intent: - **``**: A small round world with fruit trees, blue blobs, and red blobs. User tunes rules, presses play, watches the three groups rise and fall. Should feel like a tabletop world with moving bean-shaped characters, visible fruit, live controls, and charts that tell the story. - **``**: Creative freedom over layout, controls, visuals, algorithms, technical approach. "This prompt gives direction, not a strict checklist. The important part is that the world feels alive, the numbers come from the simulation, and the user can understand cause and effect." - **``**: Round 3D-looking map like a tiny raised garden dish; draggable to rotate; trees/bushes with green fruit; blue and red glossy oval blobs with simple faces; soft shadows, depth, bouncing, blinking, leaning, personality; click a blob to inspect. Food attached to plants — when a blob uses fruit the plant visibly has less, then regrows. - **``**: Each blob has energy. Moving uses energy; waiting uses a little; blue restores from fruit; red restores after gentle contact with blue; making a new blob uses stored energy; fruit returns slowly. Must create natural waves (more fruit → more blue; more blue → more red; too many red → blue drops; blue rare → red fades). **"Do not fake the chart curves. The waves should come from the energy rules."** - **``**: Blobs visibly choose actions. Blue: look for fruit, gather near trees, wander, avoid crowded areas, move away from red. Red: look for blue, wander when none near, pause after contact. Eating/contact get short cute animations (pause, chew, bounce, glow, sparkle, fruit shrink, energy pulse) and these pauses must affect behavior so actions can't instantly repeat. - **``**: Fruit growth speed, fruit limit, fruit return delay, blue energy use/speed/vision/copy threshold/eating time, red energy use/speed/vision/contact strength/copy threshold/pause time, starting fruit trees/blue/red, world size, random seed, simulation speed. Plus play, pause, step, reset, randomize, and presets: balanced garden, fruit-rich garden, red-heavy garden, fragile balance, low-fruit garden. - **``**: Real charts from recorded history. Main chart shows fruit + blue + red on one timeline with readable scaling keeping all three visible. Extras: blue-vs-red phase plot, run summary, trait trends if blobs inherit traits. Summary can say things like "The garden stayed balanced", "Blue blobs grew first, then red blobs followed", "Low fruit kept the garden small", "One group faded and the world settled into a simpler state." - **``**: Clicking a blob shows group color, energy, age, current action, speed, sensing range, time left in eating/pause animation, traits/family info. - **``**: Must demonstrate long-running waves; a fruit-rich setting where blue grows quickly; a low-fruit setting where the garden stays small; a red-heavy setting where blue dips first and red fades later; group sizes that level out instead of growing forever. Prioritize believable emergent behavior, clear controls, readable charts, charming map animation. **Explicit constraints (verbatim, must be preserved):** - *"Work only inside the current working directory. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."* - *"During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9217, then use that port for runtime verification."* - *"Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm."* - *"Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title."* → Title is exactly **"Opus 5"** in both places, nothing appended. - *"Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory."* Also from global CLAUDE.md: **NEVER use `rm -rf`** — use `trash` instead. 2. **Key Technical Concepts:** - Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript 6, pnpm, port 9217 (`strictPort` on both `server` and `preview`). - Deterministic seeded simulation: mulberry32 RNG, fixed timestep `DT = 1/30`, separate RNG streams for world creation (`seed`) and stepping (`seed ^ 0x9e3779b9`). - Spatial hash grid for neighbor queries; agent behavior state machine with locked actions. - **Predator–prey ecology theory applied deliberately**: Lotka–Volterra instability, paradox of enrichment, Holling type-II functional response, handling time (redPause), prey refuge (canopy shelter), Beddington–DeAngelis predator mutual interference, landscape-of-fear collapse, hunger-modulated risk-taking. - **Break-even prey density vs carrying capacity ratio** — the central diagnostic this session: red's break-even was ~4.3 blobs vs blue's K ≈ 52 (13:1), which guarantees prey extinction. Target was to raise it to ~40-60% of K. - Inheritable traits (speed, vision, thrift) with mutation; **cost-of-trait** economics (quadratic effort against species base speed; vision surcharge) to prevent evolutionary runaway. - History with adaptive decimation; analysis via moving average, prominence-filtered peak finding, cross-correlation phase lag. - 2.5D canvas rendering: yaw rotation + tilt foreshortening, painter's-algorithm depth sort, render interpolation via `px/py` and `advance()` alpha. - `dataviz` skill rules: **never dual-axis**, validated palette (ran `validate_palette.js`, did not eyeball), legend always for ≥2 series, selective direct labels, hairline gridlines, table-view twin, hover crosshair/tooltip, `tabular-nums` only in aligned columns. 3. **Files and Code Sections:** **Simulation (pre-existing, modified this session):** - **`src/sim/world.ts`** — the heart. Key changes this session: - `CONST` changed from `as const` to a mutable object, plus a tuning hook: ```ts /** Tuning hook for the headless probe. Never called by the app. */ export function overrideConst(patch: Partial) { Object.assign(CONST, patch) } ``` - `contactEfficiency: 1.9` → **`1.6`**; `idleUpkeep: 0.4` → **`0.28`**; added **`visionCost: 0.35`**. - **The upkeep rework (the session's most important fix)**, replacing the free-speed-trait bug: ```ts // Upkeep. Effort is measured against the *species* speed, not the blob's own // top speed, so a blob born fast genuinely pays for it — otherwise the speed // trait is free and blue simply evolves out of red's reach. Squaring it makes // sprinting expensive and idling cheap, which is what lets a hungry red blob // coast through a lean patch instead of burning itself out hunting. const base = b.kind === 'blue' ? params.blueSpeed : params.redSpeed const effort = base > 0 ? Math.hypot(b.vx, b.vy) / base : 0 const jostle = b.kind === 'red' ? 1 + CONST.interferenceCost * b.crowding : 1 const senses = 1 + CONST.visionCost * (b.traits.vision - 1) const upkeep = ((b.kind === 'blue' ? params.blueUpkeep : params.redUpkeep) * jostle * senses) / b.traits.thrift b.energy -= upkeep * (CONST.idleUpkeep + (1 - CONST.idleUpkeep) * effort * effort) * dt ``` - Red conserve behavior at the end of `stepRed`: ```ts // With nothing in sight a lean red blob stops burning energy it cannot spare // and drifts instead. Coasting through a thin patch rather than sprinting // through it is what carries red across the troughs between blue waves. const thin = 1 - clamp01(b.energy / (CONST.maxEnergy * 0.5)) const cruise = action === 'hunt' ? maxSpeed : maxSpeed * (0.72 - 0.34 * thin) ``` - Added shared helper `function clamp01(v: number) { return v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v }` and used it at the `hunger` computation (line ~543). - **`src/sim/params.ts`** — `DEFAULT_PARAMS.redVision: 95` → **`45`**. Other defaults unchanged: `fruitGrowth: 0.2, fruitLimit: 8, fruitDelay: 4, blueUpkeep: 2.6, blueSpeed: 24, blueVision: 90, blueCopy: 78, blueEatTime: 1.6, redUpkeep: 1.4, redSpeed: 29, redStrength: 12, redCopy: 84, redPause: 4, trees: 20, blueStart: 30, redStart: 8, worldSize: 330, seed: 20260725`. **`PRESETS` (balanced / fruit-rich / red-heavy / fragile / low-fruit) have NOT been retuned since the ecology rework** — `red-heavy` still overrides `redVision: 105` and `redStrength: 44`, `fragile` still has `redStrength: 40`, both now far off-scale relative to the reworked defaults. - **`scripts/probe.ts`** — headless tuner, substantially extended: - Imports `import { CONST, overrideConst } from '../src/sim/world'`. - `const BASE_CONST = { ...CONST }`, `type Knob = ParamKey | keyof typeof CONST`, and: ```ts /** Sweeps address rule constants and player params through one namespace. */ function applyKnob(key: Knob, value: number, params: Params) { if (key in params) (params as Record)[key] = value else if (key in BASE_CONST) overrideConst({ [key]: value }) else throw new Error(`unknown knob: ${key}`) } ``` - `runScan(a, b, seedCount, total)` — 2D grid scan printing `coexist/N (mean blue/red)` per cell; invoked via `--scan k=v1,v2 --scan2 k=v1,v2`. - `applyFixedConsts()` for `--const interferenceCost=1.2,shelterFactor=0.15`. - `--trace` now prints blue/red trait means (`spd/vis/thr`) per 20s slice. **New files created this session:** - **`src/theme.ts`** — validated shared palette: ```ts export const SERIES = { fruit: { light: '#00947a', dark: '#23ab92' }, blue: { light: '#3f6bd8', dark: '#6285dd' }, red: { light: '#d64533', dark: '#e05a4e' }, } as const ``` Plus `SERIES_LABEL`, `seriesColor(key, mode)`, an explicit `GardenTheme` type, `GARDEN: Record` scenery colors (sky/dishRim/dishSide/soil/soilLight/grass/grassDark/trunk/trunkDark/leaf/leafDark/leafLight/shadow), and `gardenTheme(mode)`. - **`src/render/camera.ts`** — `Camera {yaw, tilt, scale, cx, cy}`, `makeCamera()` (yaw 0.5, tilt 0.54), `project(cam,x,y,z)` returning `{sx, sy, depth}` where depth is the rotated y for painter sorting, and `unproject(cam,sx,sy)`. - **`src/render/scene.ts`** — `drawScene`, `fitCamera`, `pickBlob`, plus internal `drawDish` (blurred drop shadow, extruded rim between two ellipses, radial soil gradient, grass fringe), `drawTree` (tapered trunk with sway, 5 canopy lobes, depth-sorted fruit at anchors with gloss), `drawBlob` (gait hop, squash/stretch, gradient body, gloss, selection ring, glow, energy pip), `drawFace` (blink/eyes/pupils, chewing mouth, scared o), `drawEffect` (eat/ripen sparkles, contact ring, birth pop, death fade). All shadows drawn before any actor. Blink driven from wall clock: `const cycle = (clock * 0.3 + b.blinkTimer) % 1; drawFace(ctx, b, rw, rh, cycle < 0.05)`. - **`src/components/Garden.tsx`** — canvas with DPR scaling, single rAF loop calling `engine.advance(dt)` then `drawScene`, ResizeObserver, drag-to-rotate (`cam.yaw += dx * 0.006`), click-without-drag → `pickBlob`. - **`src/components/charts/TimelineChart.tsx`** — single-axis multi-series line chart. `indexed` prop rescales each series to its own peak (the sanctioned alternative to dual-axis). Hover crosshair + tooltip via binary search, direct end labels, `niceTicks`, `fmtTime`. - **`src/components/charts/PhasePlot.tsx`** — blue vs red path with current-position dot. - **`src/components/charts/TraitChart.tsx`** — small multiples, 3 rows (Speed/Vision/Thrift), blue+red lines, 1.0 baseline gridline, shared 0.5–1.8 range. - **`src/components/Controls.tsx`** — transport (Play/Pause, Step, Reset, Randomize), speed chips `[0.5,1,2,4,8]`, preset list, and all `PARAM_GROUPS` sliders with labels/hints/`on reset` badges. - **`src/components/Inspector.tsx`** — energy bar with copy-threshold mark, `ACTION_TEXT` map, rows for energy/copies-at/doing/age/speed/sensing range/animation left/recovering/under cover/rivals nearby/meals/children/generation/parent/born at/alive for, plus inherited-trait bars. - **`src/components/ChartsPanel.tsx`** — assembles Legend (with `keys` prop), TimelineChart with Counts/Share-of-peak/Table toggles, `summarise()` output panel, PhasePlot and TraitChart pair. Shows a nudge to the indexed view when `spread > 6`. - **`src/App.tsx`** — replaced Vite starter. Engine in a ref, `useSyncExternalStore`, `usePrefersDark`, 120ms tick for readouts, `sameParams` (ignores seed) for active-preset detection, setup params trigger `engine.reset`, topbar `

` with Time/Fruit/Blue/Red stats, three-area grid layout (stage/side/story). - **`src/App.css`** — full stylesheet with light/dark token sets under `.app` / `.app[data-mode='dark']`. - **`src/index.css`** — reduced to a minimal reset. - **`src/sim/sim.test.ts`** — new test suite: determinism (identical replay, seed divergence, manual stepping matches headless), energy rules (blue starves with no fruit, red dies without blue, blue grows in fruit-rich, levels off instead of growing forever, eating/contact tallies), garden holds together (balanced preset both alive, ≥2 waves, low-fruit smaller than fruit-rich, never exceeds population cap), traits (`costOver()` proves fast blobs pay more), analysis (bestLag finds shifted waves, summarise returns tone 'faded'), params (clampParam). - **`package.json`** scripts: ```json {"dev":"vite --port 9217","build":"tsc -b && vite build","lint":"oxlint","preview":"vite preview --port 9217","probe":"tsx scripts/probe.ts","test":"vitest run","typecheck":"tsc -b --noEmit"} ``` 4. **Errors and fixes:** - **`--scan` cells reused mutated CONST across runs** → added `overrideConst(BASE_CONST)` + `applyFixedConsts()` reset before each run in both `runScan` and the `--sweep` path. - **Free speed/vision traits** — `speedFrac = |v| / maxSpeed` where maxSpeed included `traits.speed`, so the trait cost nothing and blue would evolve out of red's reach. 722	      sepX -= (dx / d) * w

728	  let dx = 0
729	  let dy = 0

734	    b.targetBlob = prey.id
735	    if (d <= CONST.contactReach) {
736	      const taken = Math.min(params.redStrength, Math.max(0, prey.energy))
737	      prey.energy -= params.redStrength

739	      prey.glow = 0.5
740	      prey.immunity = CONST.contactImmunity
741	      prey.panic = CONST.panicTime
742	      // Being touched breaks a meal off mid-chew.
743	      if (prey.action === 'eat') {
744	        prey.action = 'flee'
745	        prey.actionTimer = 0
746	      }

750	      b.squash = 0.6
751	      b.action = 'contact'
752	      b.actionTimer = CONST.contactTime
753	      b.actionTotal = CONST.contactTime + params.redPause
754	      world.totals.contacts++
755	      addEffect(world, {

757	        x: (b.x + prey.x) / 2,
758	        y: (b.y + prey.y) / 2,
759	        z: 9,

  // Red blobs (contact feeders)
  redUpkeep: number
  redSpeed: number
  redVision: number
  redStrength: number // energy moved per contact

  // World setup (applied on reset)
  trees: number
  blueStart: number

}

export type ParamKey = keyof Params

export type ParamSpec = {
  key: ParamKey
  label: string
  min: number
  max: number
  step: number
  unit?: string
  hint: string
  /** Setup params only take effect on reset. */
  setup?: boolean
  integer?: boolean
}

export const DEFAULT_PARAMS: Params = {
  fruitGrowth: 0.2,
  fruitLimit: 8,

  blueUpkeep: 2.6,

  {

    specs: [
      {
        key: 'blueUpkeep',

        min: 0.5,

    ],

  {
    title: 'Red blobs',
    caption: 'They live off contact with blue',
    specs: [
      { key: 'redUpkeep', label: 'Energy use', min: 0.5, max: 9, step: 0.1, unit: '/s', hint: 'Energy burnt per second at full speed.' },

      seed: 771244,

  {
    id: 'red-heavy',
    name: 'Red-heavy garden',
    blurb: 'A crowd of hungry red. Blue dips first, red fades after.',
    params: {
      ...DEFAULT_PARAMS,
      redStart: 30,
      blueStart: 24,
      redStrength: 44,
      redPause: 2.4,
      redVision: 105,
      trees: 13,
      seed: 5150,
    },
  },
  {
    id: 'fragile',
    name: 'Fragile balance',
    blurb: 'Big swings on a thin margin. Some seeds collapse.',
    params: {
      ...DEFAULT_PARAMS,
      fruitGrowth: 0.055,
      fruitLimit: 9,
      fruitDelay: 9,
      blueUpkeep: 3.5,
      blueVision: 110,
      redStrength: 40,
      redPause: 2.8,
      redCopy: 80,
      trees: 12,
      blueStart: 30,
      redStart: 10,
      seed: 424242,
    },
  },
  {
    id: 'low-fruit',
    name: 'Low-fruit garden',
    blurb: 'Thin food supply keeps every group small.',
    params: {
      ...DEFAULT_PARAMS,
      fruitGrowth: 0.02,
      fruitLimit: 3,
      fruitDelay: 14,
      trees: 8,
      blueStart: 18,
      redStart: 5,
      seed: 90210,
    },
  },
]

export function clampParam(key: ParamKey, value: number): number {
  const spec = PARAM_SPECS[key]
  if (!spec) return value
  const clamped = Math.min(spec.max, Math.max(spec.min, value))
  return spec.integer ? Math.round(clamped) : clamped
}

export function isSetupParam(key: ParamKey): boolean {
  return PARAM_SPECS[key]?.setup === true
}

content.text: Hypothesis was wrong — raising `redCopy` doesn't slow red down, it stops red reproducing at all (0 red everywhere, blue parked at K≈57). Red isn't overshooting; it's marginal. That points at the opposite knob: **enrichment**. Blue's carrying capacity (~57) is far above red's break-even (~16), and Rosenzweig–MacArthur says the equilibrium only stabilises when break-even sits past the hump of the prey isocline — i.e. *lowering* K stabilises.
